title: Regional token SLI prober and evacuation orchestrator
creator: Aisha Martinez
description: Build an instrumentation + dashboard + lightweight orchestrator that (1) continuously probes token-level SLIs across regions with sequence-aware traffic shapes, (2) computes regional threshold breach candidates, and (3) coordinates a graceful evacuation (drain) + temporary admit-score backoff for affected regions. This ticket contains the probe design, dashboard panels, queries, and a short evacuation orchestration playbook for SREs and on-call engineers.
background: We have intermittent regional degradations where p95/p99 token-level latency increases asymmetrically across shards and regions. Existing dashboards report aggregated token SLIs but do not synthesize sequence-length cohorts, synthetic-probe baselines, or safe evacuation signals that tie into admission controls. Recent incidents showed manual region drains caused capacity oscillation. We need a deterministic prober and an orchestrated evacuation sequence to reduce manual churn and limit collateral degradation.
goals: Continuously sample token-level SLIs (p50/p95/p99 and KV-cache hit rate) per region and sequence-cohort (short/medium/long).
Surface potential region degradation candidates before customer-visible errors (alertable signal within 90s of onset).
Provide a single Grafana board with a synthetic-probe baseline, cohorted heatmap, ranked region breach list, and recommended evacuation action with risk score.
Implement a simple orchestrator that can trigger a staged graceful drain (evacuation) and short-term admit-score backoff with an automatic rollback window.
success_metrics: Median time from regional SLI breach to recommended action on dashboard < 90s.
Reduction in manual full-region drains during incidents by 60% in first 3 months.
During rehearse drills, customer-visible error rate in held-out traffic decreases relative to baseline by at least 40%.
Automated evacuation/rollback fidelity: no more than 1 false-positive automated evacuation per 2500 hours of runtime (expected low trust initially).
acceptance_criteria: A Grafana board exists with the following panels: cohorted token-latency heatmap, regional breach ranker, synthetic-probe trend, admit-score and admit-rate over time, KV-prefetch hit-rate, and evacuation action widget.
Prober service emits per-region per-cohort SLIs to metrics pipeline with stable metric names and labels (region, cohort, probe-id, sequence_len_bucket).
Orchestrator can be exercised in a staging rehearsal mode that performs a dry-run (no real admission changes) and a live mode with audit logging and automatic rollback after the configured window.
Runbook steps are documented in Confluence and linked from the dashboard action widget.
Two SREs and one PM have validated the dashboard and runbook in a rehearsed failure drill.
tasks: Design probe traffic shapes and sequence-length cohorts (short < 64, medium 64-512, long >512).
Implement probe harness as a lightweight service that issues synthetic requests and records token timing and KV hits.
Add metrics exposition (counter/gauge/histogram) with labels: region, cohort, probe_version, probe_id, timestamp.
Create Grafana dashboard panels and templating variables (region, cohort, time window).
Build a small orchestrator component that reads ranked breach candidates and provides staged actions: recommendation -> dry-run -> live-evacuation with admit-score backoff -> automatic rollback.
Wire orchestration audit logs to central logging and add an approval gating (initially manual via Slack approval).
Write the evacuation runbook and rehearse in staging with SREs.
Create alert rules for early-warning signals tied to the prober metrics (pager and slack channels).
Add a lightweight chaos test that injects synthetic latency into a single region and validates prober detection and orchestrator behavior.
design_notes: Probe frequency: default 10s per cohort per region; adjustable via config per region.
To avoid probe-induced noise, probes should use reserved traffic tokens and low-rps ballast; prober must honor tenant isolation and not consume shared quotas.

Evacuation should be staged: 1) increase ingress throttling by 10%, 2) apply admit-score multiplier 0.7 for 2 minutes, 3) progressively drain long-running shards over 10 minutes. Each stage observes rollback criteria before proceeding.
We will not attempt full automated cross-region failover in v1; orchestrator will provide recommended actions + gated live mode with SRE approval.
monitoring_queries: # Synthetic probe delta vs baseline: probe_latency_p95 - synthetic_baseline_p95{version="stable",region=~"$region"}
dashboard_panels: Cohorted token-latency heatmap: rows=region, cols=sequence-cohort, cells=p95/p99 colored by delta from baseline
Regional breach ranker: table sorted by composite risk score (latency delta * KV-drop * error-rate), with quick links to shard traces
Synthetic-probe trend: time series of probe p50/p95/p99 with baseline overlay and shaded alert windows
Admission control: admit-rate + admit-score time series with suggested control actions
KV-prefetch diagnostics: hit-rate, prefetch-latency, and recent misses per region
Evacuation action widget: recommended staged action with one-click dry-run and documented risk summary
runbook_steps: 1) Confirm alert on prober dashboard and inspect cohorted heatmap for concentrated degradation.
2) Check KV-prefetch diagnostics; if hit-rate drops by >20% simultaneous with latency spike, mark as cache-stress pattern.
3) Execute dry-run evacuation for target region (no changes) and observe side effects for 2 minutes.
4) If dry-run signals no global instability, authorize live evacuation with Slack approval using dashboard button.
5) Apply staged admit-score backoff and monitor synthetic probes and customer error-rate for each 60s window.
6) If error-rate improves and global impact is acceptable, continue drain; otherwise rollback to pre-evacuation admit-score and escalate.
7) After successful stabilization, create incident summary and link probe traces and decisions to postmortem.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Probes may create false positives during planned deployments. Mitigation: tag probe runs with deploy-version and suppress alerts when active deploy flag is set.
Risk: Orchestrator misconfiguration could trigger unnecessary drains. Mitigation: require gated approval and conservative default thresholds; enable canary dry-run first.
Risk: Increased metric cardinality. Mitigation: limit cohorts and region tags; roll up nightly aggregates and use relabeling in metrics pipeline.
